Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment described in the MS section (PXD025018) is an affinity purification (AP-MS) study to identify the ERα interactome. It compares an ERα immunoprecipitation (IP) against a mock IgG control. This is a discovery-based interactome study rather than a perturbation/differential proteomics study (e.g., treated vs untreated). Therefore, it is mapped as 'un-classified' per the hard rules for non-perturbation studies.

mass spectrometry analysis on a QExactive Plus mass spectrometer
differential: Relative abundances were calculated as ratios of the intensities in ERα IP channel vs the channel corresponding to mock (IgG) pulldown
peptide ratios were aggregated to the protein levels using median values of the log2 ratios
search_parameters: Carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues, and TMT labeling of lysine residues and N-terminus of the protein were allowed as fixed modifications

N-acetylation of the N-terminus of the protein, loss of protein N-terminal methionine, pyroglutamate formation from of peptide N-terminal glutamines, oxidation of methionine were allowed as variable modifications
Enzyme specificity was set as Trypsin, and up to 2 missed cleavages per peptide were allowed
